messages:
Sophia: :rotating_light: Customer reports: high p95/p99 for text-generation endpoint since 09:10 UTC, lots of timeouts and long tails. Sample req ids: r-98a1, r-98a7, r-98b2. Happening across multiple regions (us-west/us-east). No code changes on customer side. Any recent deploys?
Ethan: Not aware of app deploys around that time. Checking infra alerts now.
infra-bot: [09:14] Alert: route:/v1/generate p99 latency > 5s for 5m (us-west-2). Admission queue depth rising on pool-generic-1. CPU on worker-gpu-12 at 92%.
Priya: Sounds like request pileup / admission control kicking in. Can you grab the admission metrics and the worker queue lengths? Also any change to concurrency caps or new model variants?
Sophia: Pulling logs from support repro steps. Customer says they sent burst of long-context requests (~3k tokens). Will paste sample payload ID.
Sophia: ```
REQUEST_ID: r-98a1
model: gptx-4-8k
seq_len: 3100
tokens_out: ~1200
latency_seen: 7.8s
```
Ethan: That model's KV cache footprint is larger — fewer in-flight streams per GPU. If many long requests hit at once, admission will queue. Check admission_control decisions: `/api/debug/admission?pool=pool-generic-1&since=09:00`.
Marco: I'm seeing a sudden drop in steady-state worker concurrency beginning at 09:11 — some workers dropped from 8->4 in-flight due to OOMs and were restarting. Crash logs: ``OOM while allocating KV cache``. Restart churn caused reduced capacity and the admission queue grew.
Priya: OOMs correlate with a recent change to default quantization profile rolled last night (PR #4823). That profile increases activation memory for gptx-4-8k to improve quality. Could explain the reduced headroom.
Ethan: Good catch. We should immediately patch: rollback quant profile for that model on prod pools, and increase admission concurrency temporarily to shed queue growth. But raising concurrency might increase OOM risk — do in small increments.
Sophia: Customer impact: multiple requests failed with 502/timeout. Customer wants ETA. I told them we're investigating and will apply mitigations.
Marco: Proposed immediate mitigations (in order):
1) Patch model quant profile -> revert to previous profile for gptx-4-8k on pool-generic-1
2) Add a soft limit to burst concurrency per-tenant so a single customer can't saturate pool during recovery
3) Temporarily enable fallback-routing to smaller model variant (gptx-4-2k) for longer sequences to reduce memory pressure
4) Reboot OOMing workers after draining (kubectl cordon -> restart)
Priya: I'll run the rollback for the quant profile and flip fallback-routing. Doing a canary on 2 workers first.
Priya: Executing: ``kubectl apply -f /manifests/models/gptx-4-8k/quant-revert.yaml --context=prod``
infra-bot: [09:26] Deploy job started: quant-revert gptx-4-8k -> pool-generic-1 (canary workers: worker-21, worker-22)
Ethan: While that's going, add an admission throttle policy tweak: increase queue timeout to 45s and lower per-req concurrency weight for long-context requests. Command to update policy: ``curl -X POST https://admin.internal/admission/policy -d '{"pool":"pool-generic-1","queue_timeout_ms":45000,"long_request_weight":0.5}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'``
Marco: I'm increasing per-tenant burst cap from 200 -> 50 requests to protect other tenants. Applied via tenant-config API.
Sophia: Communicated to customer: "We've identified memory pressure from a model quant change; applying mitigations (rollback + fallback) and will monitor. ETA ~30-45m." They replied :thumbsup: asking for progress updates.
infra-bot: [09:34] Canary revert applied successfully on worker-21, worker-22. KV allocations within expected ranges. No OOMs on canary.
Priya: Rolling out revert to remaining workers in pool-generic-1 but pacing at 3 workers/min to avoid further churn.
Ethan: Also enabling temporary routing fallback for requests with seq_len > 2500 to gptx-4-2k: ``route.rule(seq_len>2500) -> model=gptx-4-2k, fallback=true``. That should reduce memory per request.
Marco: After the first 10 reverted workers, p95 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.2s and p99 from 7.1s -> 2.8s in us-west. Queue depth decreased by ~70%.
Sophia: Customer updated: latency improved, some requests still slow but majority ok. They appreciate the quick response.
Priya: Monitoring for 30m. If we stay stable, we'll keep the revert and plan a safer quant rollout with resource limits and perf tests. Also propose adding regression alert that ties model quant/profile changes to OOM rate increases.
Marco: Action items:
- Priya: Keep revert rolling and monitor (in progress)
- Ethan: Add temporary per-tenant burst cap (done) and watch throttled customers list
- Sophia: Collect customer logs for any remaining failures and send postmortem notice once stable
- Marco: Create follow-up bug to add model-profile safety checks to rollout pipeline (ticket INF-3247)
Sophia: Thanks team. I'll update the customer thread and set follow-up check at +60m.
infra-bot: [10:10] Alert cleared: route:/v1/generate p99 latency back within bounds (5m avg).
